title: PR #412: coupons, idempotent charges, refunds on cancel
summary: Adds coupon discounts to order creation, makes charge() idempotent on order id, and refunds the charge when an order is cancelled. Two request flows change: create order and cancel order.
other: Order dataclass gains discount and charge_id fields (shop/orders.py)
No tests added for apply_coupon, charge idempotency, or refund

flows.title: Create order
flows.description: POST /orders, called by the checkout page. Promises a saved order that is paid for and has its stock reserved. This PR inserts a coupon step before stock reservation and makes the charge idempotent on the order id.

nodes.label: POST /orders → create_order()
nodes.change: applies coupon, stores charge_id, returns discount
nodes.notes: InvalidCoupon is not caught here or in any middleware shown in the diff, so a bad coupon code becomes a 500 rather than a 400.

nodes.label: apply_coupon()
nodes.change: discounts total by coupon rate, raises InvalidCoupon
notes: Lookup is case-insensitive via upper(); COUPONS has no expiry or usage cap.
Mutates order.total in place, so everything downstream (stock, charge, response) sees the discounted total. Intended, but worth confirming.
nodes.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+COUPONS = {"WELCOME10": 0.10, "VIP25": 0.25}
+
+
+class InvalidCoupon(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def apply_coupon(order, code: str | None):
+    if not code:
+        return order
+    rate = COUPONS.get(code.upper())
+    if rate is None:
+        raise InvalidCoupon(code)
+    order.discount = round(order.total * rate, 2)
+    order.total = round(order.total - order.discount, 2)
+    return order

nodes.label: charge()
nodes.notes: _seen is a module-level dict: idempotency does not survive a restart and is not shared across replicas. Fine for a single process, misleading otherwise.
nodes.diff:
@@ -1,5 +1,15 @@
 import gateway
 
+_seen: dict[str, str] = {}
 
-def charge(customer_id: str, amount: float) -> str:
-    return gateway.charge(customer_id, amount)
+
+def charge(customer_id: str, amount: float, idempotency_key: str) -> str:
+    if idempotency_key in _seen:
+        return _seen[idempotency_key]
+    charge_id = gateway.charge(customer_id, amount)
+    _seen[idempotency_key] = charge_id
+    return charge_id

nodes.label: save_order()
nodes.notes: Unchanged, but now persists the new discount and charge_id fields because Order is stored whole.

flows.title: Cancel order
flows.description: POST /orders/:id/cancel, called from the account page and by support tooling. Promises released stock and a cancelled status. This PR inserts a refund branch between releasing stock and saving the status.

nodes.label: POST /orders/:id/cancel → cancel_order()
nodes.change: refunds the charge before marking cancelled
nodes.notes: If refund() raises, stock is already released and the status is never saved: the order stays 'new' with its stock gone. Consider refunding before release_stock or saving status first.
nodes.diff:
@@ -16,6 +19,8 @@ def cancel_order(req):
 def cancel_order(req):
     order = load_order(req.params["id"])
     release_stock(order)
+    if order.charge_id:
+        refund(order.charge_id)
     order.status = "cancelled"
     save_order(order)
     return {"status": order.status}

nodes.label: load_order()
nodes.notes: Unchanged, but orders saved before this deploy have no charge_id, so cancelling them skips the refund branch. Needs a backfill or a fallback lookup.

nodes.label: refund()
nodes.notes: No idempotency guard, unlike charge(). A retried cancel refunds twice.

nodes.label: gateway.refund()
nodes.notes: gateway is not in this repo. Confirm refund() exists on it; the diff adds the call without touching the gateway module.
